name: BQ24073RGTR
title: BQ2407x: 1.5 A single-cell Li-ion linear charger with power-path management, VQFN-16
summary: The BQ2407x family (BQ24072, BQ24073, BQ24074, BQ24075, BQ24079) are standalone linear chargers for one Li-ion cell with a power path: OUT feeds the system from the input while the battery charges separately, and the battery tops up OUT when the input cannot keep up. They run from USB (100 mA or 500 mA limit with VIN-DPM) or an adapter, with a resistor-set input limit and charge current up to 1.5 A, 28 V input rating and overvoltage protection. Resistors set charge current, input limit and timers; pin 15 is TD, ITERM or SYSOFF depending on the device. The BQ24073 regulates OUT to 4.4 V and the battery to 4.2 V, with a 6.6 V OVP threshold.
key_figures: 100 mA, 500 mA or KILIM/RILIM up to 1.5 A

notes: The device options BQ24072 to BQ24079T differ in input overvoltage threshold, battery regulation voltage, OUT regulation, DPPM threshold and the function of pin 15; the device comparison table lists them.
BQ24075 also exists as an automotive-qualified BQ24075-Q1.
A marking in parentheses with a comma lists alternatives; one of them appears on a given part.

pins.name: BAT

circuits.title: Typical application circuit (BQ24075, BQ24079)
circuits.description: A standalone BQ24075/BQ24079 charger. EN2 is tied to OUT and EN1 to ground, so the input limit comes from the 1.18 kΩ ILIM resistor; the 1.13 kΩ ISET resistor sets fast charge. CE grounded keeps charging enabled and TMR grounded turns the safety timers off. An outside ON/OFF signal drives SYSOFF to cut the battery from the system. Two LEDs with 1 kΩ resistors from OUT show power good and charging. The pack's NTC sits on TS.

operation.text: The BQ2407x is a single-cell Li-ion linear charger with a power path. FET Q1 runs from IN to OUT and feeds the system; FET Q2 runs between BAT and OUT and charges or discharges the cell. Input current is shared between system and battery, and the system is served first, so the system runs at once from a flat or missing battery and the cell sees fewer cycles.

Below UVLO the part is powered down: control pins are ignored, Q1 is off, CHG and PGOOD are high impedance and Q2 is on (off if SYSOFF is high), with the OUT short-circuit monitor active. Between UVLO and VBAT + VIN(DT) the part sleeps with the same state; after more than 20 ms in sleep the IN-to-OUT path is cut, so a grounded input draws nothing from the battery beyond BAT leakage.

When VIN exceeds VBAT + VIN(DT), PGOOD goes low and CE, EN1, EN2 are read. EN1 = EN2 = high, or an input overvoltage, gives standby: Q1 off, OUT fed from the battery. Otherwise, with the input valid (above UVLO and VBAT + VIN(DT), below VOVP), the part checks ISET and ILIM for shorts, then turns Q1 on with a 100 mA limit to test OUT for a short. Once VOUT passes VO(SC1) the limit set by EN1, EN2 and RILIM takes over and normal running begins.

IN tolerates 28 V. If VIN stays above VOVP longer than tDGL(OVP), the input LDO turns off and charging stops; OUT is fed from the battery and PGOOD goes high impedance. When the overvoltage clears a fresh power-up runs, the safety timers restart and CHG shows the new charge cycle.

operation.topic: Input current limit and USB inrush
operation.text: EN1 and EN2 pick a 100 mA (USB100) or 500 mA (USB500) limit, a limit set by RILIM up to 1.5 A, or suspend. The start-up current limit holds inrush within the USB-IF figure of 50 µC above 100 mA even with more than 10 µF on OUT; capacitance directly on IN is not limited and is kept under 10 µF for that reason.

In USB100 and USB500 modes the input voltage is watched. A sag to VIN-DPM makes the part pull its input limit down and hold the voltage there, so a weak or current-limited USB port is not pulled down.

If system load plus charge current exceeds the input limit, OUT falls. When OUT reaches VDPPM the charger cuts charge current as system current rises, keeping OUT up. Termination is off while DPPM is active.

If charge current has fallen to zero and the load still exceeds the input limit, OUT drops further; below VBSUP1 the battery supplies the shortfall through Q2, fully on and unregulated, until OUT recovers above VBSUP2. If OUT falls VO(SC2) below BAT and stays there past tDGL(SC2), OUT shuts off and is retried after tREC(SC2), repeating while the short lasts. Termination is off in this mode.

OUT is regulated to a fixed VO(REG) on BQ24073, BQ24074 (4.4 V) and BQ24075, BQ24079 (5.5 V). On the BQ24072 OUT follows the battery at about VBAT + 225 mV, held at 3.4 V while the battery is below 3.2 V so the load can start from a flat cell.

With no input, OUT is fed from the battery with no current regulation; the short-circuit monitor still turns OUT off when it falls 250 mV below BAT for tDGL(SC2) and retries after tREC(SC2) until the overload is gone.

CE low starts charging. The part first sources IBAT(SC) into BAT and waits for VBAT(SC) to rule out a shorted battery. Then: pre-charge at IPRECHG until VBAT crosses VLOWV, constant-current fast charge at ICHG, and constant voltage at VBAT(REG) while current tapers. When current reaches ITERM, CHG goes high impedance. Termination is suspended whenever the thermal, DPPM or VIN-DPM loop is lowering the charge current.
If ICHG is set above the input limit, the battery charges at IIN(MAX) less the OUT load, and the safety timers run proportionally slower.

TD high disables termination: the charger runs pre-charge, fast charge and then stays in constant voltage at VBAT(REG) indefinitely, at the lower of ICHG and IINmax. Battery detection and the safety timers are off. CHG goes high impedance once current drops below ITERM and stays so until input power or CE is cycled. With TD high and TS open or pulled to VIN, pack temperature sensing is also off.

After a completed cycle the battery voltage is watched. Below VRCH, detection runs: IBAT(DET) is drawn for tDET; if BAT stays above VLOWV a battery is present and charging restarts. If it drops, the battery is missing or its protector is open, so pre-charge current is applied for tDET to try to close the protector; VBAT then below VRCH means charging starts, above VRCH means no battery and detection repeats.

SYSOFF high turns Q2 off and separates the battery from OUT, for cutting the load from the cell, for factory programming without a battery, or for a host-side fuel gauge that needs the open-circuit voltage. CHG stays low while SYSOFF is high. SYSOFF to VSS is normal running; an internal pull-up of about 5 MΩ goes to VBAT.

Pre-charge and fast-charge timers start with their phases. TMR open gives defaults (1800 s and 18000 s typ); a resistor sets them by Equations 6 and 7; TMR at VSS disables them. Toggling CE or entering and leaving USB suspend resets them. They pause in thermal shutdown and slow in proportion to charge current under DPPM, VIN-DPM or thermal regulation: half the current for two minutes counts as one minute. If pre-charge does not reach VLOWV, or the fast-charge timer runs out with current still above ITERM, CHG flashes at about 2 Hz; CE or input toggling, suspend, or an OVP event clears the fault.

PGOOD is low while VBAT + VIN(DT) < VIN < VOVP. CHG turns on (low) for the first charge after power-up, after CE goes low, or after leaving OVP; later refresh charges leave it off. Timer faults flash CHG at about 2 Hz. A pack temperature fault suspends charging while CHG stays low.

Above TJ(REG) the charge current is reduced to hold the die temperature. If the die still reaches TJ(OFF), typically under high VIN and heavy OUT load, Q1 turns off and Q2 on so the battery carries the load; after cooling by TJ(OFF-HYS) Q1 returns. Sustained overheating gives a hiccup cycle. Termination is off during thermal regulation and the timers slow in step with the current.

While charging, INTC flows out of TS into the pack NTC. If VTS leaves the window between VHOT and VCOLD, charging pauses and the timers hold; it resumes when VTS returns. With a 103AT-2 thermistor the window is 0 °C to 50 °C; Rs and Rp (Equations 8, 9) can widen it but not narrow it. On BQ24072 and BQ24073, sensing is off when TD is high and VTS is above VDIS(TS). A 10 kΩ resistor from TS to VSS replaces the thermistor where sensing is not wanted.

The charger stays on for at least 20 ms typical after the input drops into sleep, so adapters with half-wave rectification on 50 Hz mains can be used. The input must not fall below UVLO; a battery above UVLO helps, and more input capacitance may be needed.

The example runs from 5 V with about 800 mA fast charge (ISET, pin 16), 1.3 A input limit (ILIM, pin 12), 110 mA termination on BQ24074 (ITERM, pin 15), a 6.25 h fast-charge timer (TMR, pin 14) and a 10 kΩ 103AT-2 NTC on TS.
For indicators, a 1.5 kΩ resistor and an LED in series go from OUT to CHG and from OUT to PGOOD. For a processor, each output gets a pull-up of about 100 kΩ to the processor rail.

Ceramic decoupling on IN, OUT and BAT at the application-circuit values is the starting point; DC loads may allow values toward the minimum, fast large pulsed loads may need more. Capacitors on IN must be rated for the highest input a faulty adapter can apply; ceramics are tested at twice rating, so a 16 V part may survive a 30 V transient if its maker confirms the test rating.

Place the IN and OUT decoupling capacitors as close to the IC as possible, with short traces to IN, OUT and the thermal pad. Keep low-current ground returns apart from the battery's high-current paths and join them at a single point. Size the IN and OUT traces for the full charge current. The thermal pad is the main ground and heat path and is soldered to board ground; the example layout puts six vias in it.

Dissipation peaks early in the charge, when the battery is lowest; after fast charge starts the pack typically reaches about 3.4 V within two minutes, while the assembly takes a few minutes to heat, so 3.4 V is a fair minimum for worst-case dissipation by Equation 11. Normal input and ambient conditions should not drive the part into thermal regulation; it remains functional if they do.
A full 1000 mAh cell with 10 µA of BAT leakage would take 100000 hours (11.4 years) to discharge; typical cell self-discharge is about five times that leakage.
